top_story.headline: Rep. Laurel Lee's Spouse's Bank of America Sale Disclosed 53 Days After the Trade
top_story.dek: The periodic transaction report was filed eight days past the STOCK Act's 45-day window.
paragraphs: Rep. Laurel Lee (FL-15) filed a periodic transaction report on October 16 showing two transactions in accounts marked as owned by her spouse. One was a late disclosure: a sale of Bank of America Corporation common stock worth $50,001 to $100,000 on August 24, reported 53 days later, eight days beyond the 45-day deadline in the STOCK Act.

The same report shows a purchase of Nokia shares (ticker NOKBF) worth $15,001 to $50,000 on September 18, which was within the window. The input shows no other late trades among the three House filings reviewed today, and the Office of Government Ethics summary reports only routine annual disclosures.

sections.headline: No FARA contacts today; one lobbying filing names the Office of the Vice President
paragraphs: No new FARA filings turned up in the top-officials search. The only match was one Lobbying Disclosure Act filing that lists the Office of the Vice President among the entities lobbied.

items: Building and Construction Trades Department, AFL-CIO (in-house, 3rd Quarter report) lists the Office of the Vice President among the entities lobbied. Issues named include H.R. 3548, the Infrastructure Expansion Act (a bill on liability for property owners and contractors on federally assisted infrastructure projects), the Surface Transportation Reauthorization, and S.J. Res. 37, a joint resolution terminating the national emergency declared to impose duties on articles imported from Canada. Filing.

sections.headline: One stock-trade report with a late disclosure, plus two candidate reports
paragraphs: Three House filings were new since the last edition and no Senate filings were. One is a periodic transaction report with two parsed trades, one of them late. The other two are candidate reports.

items: Rep. Laurel Lee (FL-15), periodic transaction report filed October 16: two transactions in spouse-owned accounts. A sale of Bank of America Corporation stock on August 24 ($50,001 to $100,000) was disclosed 53 days later, a late disclosure eight days past the 45-day limit. A purchase of Nokia shares on September 18 ($15,001 to $50,000) was within the window. Filing.
